root_cause.text: The FI_NO_EXTENT flag was not set before clearing extent nodes in __destroy_extent_node(), allowing concurrent writeback threads to insert new extent nodes into the tree while destruction was in progress, causing a race condition that violates the node_cnt invariant.
root_cause.evidence: The patch shows that FI_NO_EXTENT is now set under et->lock within the while loop in __destroy_extent_node() (lines 647-648), and the check for FI_NO_EXTENT in __update_extent_tree_range() is moved outside the type-specific condition (lines 694-697) to protect both EX_READ and EX_BLOCK_AGE extent tree updates. The CVE description explicitly demonstrates the race: concurrent writeback can call __update_extent_tree_range() to insert new nodes while __destroy_extent_node() is freeing nodes, since FI_NO_EXTENT was never set to prevent new insertions. The fix ensures FI_NO_EXTENT is set consistently across all callers before any extent tree modifications occur.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix extent tree initialization to respect FI_NO_EXTENT flag for all extent types, not just read operations.
intent_record.what: Moved the `is_inode_flag_set(inode, FI_NO_EXTENT)` check from inside the `if (type == EX_READ)` block to before it, making it apply to all extent types rather than only EX_READ.
intent_record.how: Previously, the FI_NO_EXTENT flag check only prevented extent tree usage when type was EX_READ. Now it prevents extent tree usage for all extent types (EX_READ, EX_WRITE, etc.). This causes the function to return false earlier and more broadly when the FI_NO_EXTENT flag is set on an inode.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a guard to set the FI_NO_EXTENT inode flag during extent tree destruction, with a conditional check to avoid redundant operations.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional check inside the while loop that sets the FI_NO_EXTENT inode flag if it is not already set, before calling __free_extent_tree().
intent_record.how: This change ensures that the FI_NO_EXTENT flag is set on the inode during extent tree destruction. The conditional prevents redundant flag-setting operations by only calling set_inode_flag() when the flag is not already present, avoiding unnecessary writes when the flag state is already correct.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix extent tree update logic by checking FI_NO_EXTENT flag unconditionally for all extent types, not just EX_READ operations.

intent_record.how: This change causes the early return when FI_NO_EXTENT flag is set to apply to all callers regardless of the extent type parameter, rather than only for EX_READ operations. This prevents unnecessary processing of the extent tree for any operation when the no-extent flag is active.

This is a different problem than the race condition described in the root cause.

candidates.rationale: This loop attempts to destroy extent nodes without first setting the FI_NO_EXTENT flag. Without this flag being set before the loop begins, concurrent writeback threads can insert new extent nodes into the tree during destruction, causing the node_cnt invariant to be violated as nodes are being freed while new ones are being added.

The __free_extent_tree() call proceeds without the FI_NO_EXTENT flag being set, allowing the extent tree to remain open for concurrent modifications. This enables race conditions where new extent nodes can be inserted by writeback threads while the tree is being destroyed, violating the node_cnt invariant.

vuln_statements.explanation: This loop attempts to destroy extent nodes without first setting the FI_NO_EXTENT flag on the inode. Without this flag being set before entering the loop, concurrent writeback threads can insert new extent nodes into the tree during destruction, causing a race condition where node_cnt is decremented by __free_extent_tree() while simultaneously being incremented by concurrent insertions, violating the node_cnt invariant.

The __free_extent_tree() call proceeds without the FI_NO_EXTENT flag being set beforehand, leaving the extent tree open for concurrent modifications. This allows writeback threads to insert new extent nodes into the tree while it is being destroyed, creating a race condition that violates the node_cnt invariant as nodes are freed while new ones are simultaneously added.

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces a fix for the race condition vulnerability. The new __destroy_extent_node() function (lines 625-649) now implements batched extent node destruction with proper locking. Critically, the function sets the FI_NO_EXTENT flag BEFORE calling __free_extent_tree() in batches (as seen in __update_extent_tree_range at lines 805-806 and __drop_extent_tree at lines 1139-1140). The batched approach with the loop 'while (atomic_read(&et->node_cnt))' ensures that the write lock is released periodically between batches, preventing concurrent writeback threads from being blocked indefinitely. The __free_extent_tree() function is modified to accept nr_shrink parameter (line 382) and only removes up to nr_shrink nodes per call (line 390: 'for (count = 0; node && count < nr_shrink; count++)'), allowing the lock to be released and re-acquired. This prevents the race condition where new extent nodes could be inserted while the tree was being destroyed, as the FI_NO_EXTENT flag is set before destruction begins, and the batched approach with lock release/reacquisition prevents the invariant violation.
